title: A singleton that stays single under threads

blocks.text: The page's interview answer builds a singleton from access modifiers: a **private constructor**, a **private static** field holding the one instance, and a **public static** method handing it out. It then warns that its lazy version is not thread-safe: two threads can both see `instance == null` and both construct.
`Settings` loads its values in a private constructor that is given to you and takes a moment to run. Keep that constructor as it is. Write:

items: `public static Settings getInstance()`: always returns the one `Settings` object, **also when many threads call it for the first time at once**;
`public String get(String key)`: returns the loaded value for `key`, or `null`.

blocks.text: `created()` (given) counts how many times the constructor has run.
The page names three thread-safe ways; any of them is accepted.

cases.says: getInstance returns the same Settings object on every call, and no constructor is public.
Eight threads asking for the instance at the same moment still cause exactly one construction.

concepts: A private constructor with a public static accessor makes a singleton, and its lazy form needs care to stay single under threads.
